note: Per-alias context windows (KTD7). The gateway has no window field to extend, so this table is the plugin's own. `model` records the upstream model string the alias pointed at when the entry was written — spawnctl status compares it against gateway.yaml, because the model-list endpoint returns only id and display_name and a repointed alias would otherwise drift silently. A chain alias takes the SMALLEST window across its routes, so a mid-session fallback can only under-declare rather than overflow.
families_note: The grammar the command layer reads prose against (KTD3). Everything after a command is prose; the reading agent derives a family and an optional tier from it and hands a script exactly ONE resolved alias (KD6). That derivation needs the family -> tier -> alias relation DECLARED, because it is not recoverable from the flat `aliases` map below: `k3` is relatable to `kimi` only through the upstream string `moonshotai/kimi-k3`, and `gpt` pointing at the same model as `gpt-sol` is a coincidence of how the gateway was configured, not a stated default. Inferring either is how an unserved tier silently becomes the default instead of failing loudly. `tiers` maps the tier name AS PROSE SPELLS IT (hyphens included, e.g. `sol-pro`) to the served alias; `default` is the alias a bare family name resolves to; `no_family_alias` is what prose naming no family at all resolves to. A family or tier absent from this block is UNSERVED: the command layer fails and names the served aliases rather than falling back. This block is the grammar; `aliases` stays the metadata table it already was.
chain_policy_note: Which surfaces may resolve to a chain alias (an `aliases` entry with chain:true, whose `model` is a list of routes). A chain can change model mid-flight on fallback, and this table deliberately under-declares a chain's context window to its smallest route — tolerable for one tool-less turn, wrong for an hour-long job holding tools (KTD4). `refuse` means the surface must reject the alias before any network call and say which non-chain aliases it will take.

kimi.source: upstream model card — OpenRouter listing for moonshotai/kimi-k2.7-code reports context_length 262144, read 2026-08-06. gateway.yaml carries no window comment for this alias.

k3.source: gateway.yaml comment above the alias: "1M context, but ~4x the price of K2.7 Code"; the OpenRouter listing for moonshotai/kimi-k3 pins that 1M at context_length 1048576, read 2026-08-06.

glm.source: upstream model card — OpenRouter listing for z-ai/glm-5.2 reports context_length 1048576, read 2026-08-06. gateway.yaml carries no window comment for this alias.

gpt-luna.source: gateway.yaml comment above the GPT-5.6 tiers: "all 1.05M context".

gpt-terra.source: gateway.yaml comment above the GPT-5.6 tiers: "all 1.05M context".

gpt-sol.source: gateway.yaml comment above the GPT-5.6 tiers: "all 1.05M context".

gpt-sol-pro.source: gateway.yaml comment above the GPT-5.6 tiers: "all 1.05M context"; gpt-sol-pro is the same model as gpt-sol served with reasoning.mode=pro, so it inherits the tier's window.

gpt.source: gateway.yaml comment above the GPT-5.6 tiers: "all 1.05M context"; `gpt` is the back-compat alias pointing at the same gpt-5.6-sol model as gpt-sol. It is also the DECLARED default of the `gpt` family (see `families`) — that it happens to serve the sol tier's model is no longer what makes it the default.

default.source: chain — the smallest window across its routes: kimi (262144) and glm (1048576), both from the OpenRouter listing read 2026-08-06. Under-declaring is the safe direction for a mid-session fallback.
